# Issue 31 implementation plan

SIGNAL HUNTER has two activities in one BBS door. The Chapter 2 route compares the canonical three trace cards to acquire the R07-SPOOL-02 manifest. Optional seeded practice provides three different signal-analysis challenges and keeps its own progress. The supplied base is missing the story transition that makes this door available.

WorkUnit correction: required

The WorkUnit requires the Chapter 2 story connection (`.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:23`) and a shipped, replayable door with persistent rewards and a keyboard browser journey (`.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:15,30–31`). The design grants entry only when the player restores SPOOL-02 (`docs/game-design.md:141,157–158,167`). The BBS in this base opens after Episode 000 (`content/bbs/deep-field.json:1–6`). Its existing door is Relay Trivia (`content/doors/relay-trivia.json:2–12`), the code catalog is empty (`src/doors/code-doors.ts:4`), and an inventory of grants, door rewards and event effects in all `content/**/*.json` found no restoration fact or action. A new `requires` flag with no producer fails content validation (`src/content/validate.ts:422–442,515–517`). Building the Chapter 2 recovery chain would exceed the door-only scope (`.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:19`).

Correct the WorkUnit dependency and approve a base containing the playable SPOOL-02 restoration transition. Identify its saved fact and the shared manifest reward fact in the corrected contract. This enables a real registry gate and a representative browser fixture. A test save with the gate preloaded can exercise the door in isolation. The shipped restore action is still required for the player path. Steps 1–4 below describe the bounded door work against the corrected contract. The focused checks and the blocked integration coverage are in `TEST_PLAN.md`.

## What we know

- Chapter 2 fixes the target SPOOL-02 and intact signature, H1 `RELAY-07 / INTACT`, H2 `SPOOL-02 / DAMAGED`, H3 `SPOOL-02 / INTACT`, and H3 as the sole manifest answer. Trader awards the same artifact. Either door can display it after acquisition, and additional hunting is optional (`docs/game-design.md:144,158–171,177–185`).
- `CODE_DOORS` is shared by the registry and validator. Validation reads static metadata. The registry filters the listing and lookup by facts and sends the selected lazy loader to the host (`src/content/validate.ts:82–85,147–158`, `src/doors/code-doors.ts:3–4`, `src/doors/registry.ts:9–37`).
- The save has a uint32 `profile.seed`, and the host already owns the save while invoking the registered loader. Door callbacks receive only a frozen `hasFact` query. The only `registration.load()` caller in `src`, `scripts`, and `tests` is `createDoorHost.launch` (`src/progress/save.ts:48–58,79–100`, `src/doors/host.ts:15–17,29–60`, `src/doors/contract.ts:84–89`, `tests/unit/doors.test.ts:178–194`).
- The host restores validated versioned slots and checkpoints on input and exit. It persists a checkpoint, any newly awarded declared facts and event effects together. `addFact` also deduplicates. `writeSave` and `loadSave` round-trip door payloads, and malformed slots are isolated (`src/doors/host.ts:53–60,71–105`, `src/progress/save.ts:121–150,186–190,208–214,251–255`).
- `mulberry32` is a pure deterministic primitive used by the existing waterfall generator. Door-specific interference and decoding fit alongside this reusable RNG (`src/signal/rng.ts:1–11`, `src/signal/waterfall.ts:17–31`). The terminal already prints DOM text in a focusable live log, submits keyboard commands using a labelled input, and exposes action buttons. `EXIT` is host-owned and returns to the signed-in menu (`src/terminal/terminal.ts:39–104,118–136`, `src/bbs/door-session.ts:19–50`, `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:29–72`).
- Playwright already discovers `tests/e2e` and runs the production build in Chromium under the Pages subpath by request interception. `Browser tests` runs on pull requests in Ubuntu (`playwright.config.ts:3–14`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3–5`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:5–37`, `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:1–25`).

## What we're assuming

- A monotonic saved fact will represent restoration, and a single shared `flag:` will represent manifest acquisition. `flag:spool-02-restored` and `flag:manifest-r07-spool-02` are illustrative IDs. The correction must supply the durable IDs and their producers or consumers. Verify those in the corrected base and confirm the catalog with `npm run content:validate`.
- This fits one 32-hour claim once a corrected base is approved. Estimate 8–14 hours for door logic, authored screens, unit and browser cases, review and validation. The recovery chain is outside that estimate and belongs to the dependency.

## Open questions

- Which dependency and approved base provide the playable restoration transition, and which saved fact will downstream reconstruction consume? The correction supplies those inputs. Step 3 verifies the publisher and registration metadata in source.
- Does the real Chromium journey keep the prompt focused and present the full evidence at keyboard speed through reload? Step 4 supplies the journey and the existing CI job supplies the runtime evidence. This planner has no browser grant. Firefox, Safari and other OS or harness profiles are outside the named checks.

## Architectural context and execution paths

- The native SwarmOS backend on Linux routes developer and tester work to Codex (`.swarm/config.yaml:16–18,59–67`). Node 24 runs the pure scenario code, real door host, registry and save functions in Vitest's Node project (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts:5–10`). Run persistence checks with a `SaveStorage` test double that stores serialized bytes and create a fresh host and save session on reload.
- The shipped path is the static browser client. `src/main.ts:29–40,136–159` opens a localStorage save, then passes its data and persistence callback to the registered door host in the BBS. The browser check uses GitHub Actions on `ubuntu-latest` and the existing Playwright Chromium harness. It exercises the same production path through the intercepted `/signal-lost/` assets. No service, network account or real timestamp is involved in generation or reward settlement.

## Implementation sequence for the corrected WorkUnit

### 1. Generate scenarios with one answer each

Create `src/doors/signal-hunter/generate.ts` with `generateScenario(saveSeed, difficulty, ordinal)` and the shared types for a scenario and candidate IDs. Use `mulberry32` with a stable difficulty salt and uint32 ordinal mixing. Generate three labelled candidates (`A`, `B`, `C`), each with 12 numbered windows. Each window has integer reference power and measured power. Reference power models common interference. Measured power is the reference plus a seeded baseline in `0..2` and `8` for a pulse. The published cutoff is residual `>= 8`. Keep the latent winner and pulse masks out of the text evidence and analysis inputs. Guarantee adjacent `NEW` scenarios differ in the observable samples by making the first reference reading for candidate A have the same parity as the ordinal, including at uint32 rollover. Save each practice round's ordinal and completion state, and regenerate the readings from the save seed.

| Difficulty | Published rule and necessary deduction | Construction that guarantees a unique result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EASY` | Subtract reference power window by window to find a trace with continuous residual pulses. | The correct candidate pulses at all 12 windows. Two decoys miss pulses, with one consistently louder in raw power due to stronger common interference. |
| `MEDIUM` | Find one pulse in the same position in each of four consecutive three-window blocks. | Every candidate has four pulses, one per block. Only the correct candidate maintains its seeded phase across all four. |
| `HARD` | Use the published pair encoding `pulse/quiet = 1`, `quiet/pulse = 0` and compare the resulting six bits with the printed reference signature. | Every candidate has exactly one pulse per pair. Generate the reference signature from the seed and give each decoy a differing bit sequence. Pulse count and valid pair structure do not distinguish the correct candidate. |

Create `src/doors/signal-hunter/analysis.ts` with `analyzeCandidate` and typed diagnostic results for missing continuous pulses, phase mismatch and signature mismatch. Assess each candidate from its public readings and the active rule. `SUBMIT` accepts one candidate ID, with an exact finite answer domain. The solver in `tests/unit/signal-hunter/scenarios.test.ts` independently enumerates all three IDs for at least 200 seeds per difficulty using only the player-visible readings, rules and signature. Compare the result with the set accepted by the production adjudicator. Include explicit assertions that raw power, pulse counts and valid pairs alone are insufficient in their respective modes.

### 2. Implement the door lifecycle and authored screens

- Create `src/doors/signal-hunter/index.ts` with `createSignalHunter(saveSeed, manifestFact)` built on `defineDoor`, a strict JSON `saveState` schema and a screen builder. Save the active view, per-difficulty `{ ordinal, solved }` state and a monotonic `manifestVerified` boolean. Version the slot via registration. Recreate the current challenge on restore. Use the host's invalid-slot fallback for bad payloads. Display the receipt if `progress.hasFact(manifestFact)` is already true, including visits after a Trader acquisition or a damaged local slot. `isComplete` follows `manifestVerified`, which only a canonical H3 submission sets.
- Create `content/screens/signal-hunter-brief.json`, `content/screens/signal-hunter-receipt.json` and `content/screens/signal-hunter-practice.json` using the existing `{id, lines}` schema (`src/content/schema.ts:458–461`). Author the fixed target and all three cards together, their verified receipt with SC-1, QR-1, RW-1 and preservation terms, and the practice rules including units, window numbering, pulse cutoff and bit order. Import these screen records from the lazy door module. Keep the dynamic readings and command labels in TypeScript.
- Start in the manifest view on first entry. `BRIEF` returns to it. Provide `SUBMIT H1`, `SUBMIT H2` and `SUBMIT H3` as typed commands and buttons. H1 feedback names the wrong node; H2 feedback names the damaged signature. H3 shows the signed manifest. A previously acquired manifest opens the same receipt. A practice win only marks the active practice round solved.
- Offer `PRACTICE EASY`, `PRACTICE MEDIUM`, `PRACTICE HARD`, `SCAN A`, `SCAN B`, `SCAN C`, `HELP`, `SUBMIT A/B/C` as three actions, `RETRY` and `NEW` where applicable. Label each scan window and measurement in terminal text. Show the active difficulty and round, the relevant rule and reference signature where needed. Normalize case and surrounding whitespace locally. Give a specific correction after an incorrect submission. `RETRY` clears feedback while retaining the readings and `NEW` advances just that difficulty's ordinal and clears its solved state. Empty, unknown and out-of-view submissions change no completion state. Use the host's `EXIT` action.

### 3. Register the door and bind the save seed

Modify `CodeDoorRegistration.load` in `src/doors/contract.ts:84–89` to accept `saveSeed: number`. Modify only the invocation inside `createDoorHost.launch` (`src/doors/host.ts:43–52`) to pass `data.profile.seed`. The registry already carries the loader type, and existing zero-argument registrations can ignore the extra argument. Keep lifecycle callbacks, `DoorProgress`, save schema, reward settlement and BBS routing intact.

Modify `CODE_DOORS` in `src/doors/code-doors.ts:3–4` to register ID `signal-hunter`, display name `SIGNAL HUNTER`, authored attribution, version 1, the corrected base's restoration requirement and the shared manifest reward. Set `returnTo: 'bbs-menu'`. In `load`, use a literal `import('./signal-hunter/index.ts')`, call `createSignalHunter(saveSeed, manifestFact)` and return it in the registry's `{ default }` wrapper. Keep metadata available to validation without evaluating the door module. Confirm the required fact's actual granting action and validate the bundled content.

### 4. Verify the isolated door and the BBS journey

- Create `tests/unit/signal-hunter/door.test.ts`. Use the real catalog, host, BBS session and public save functions. Use a post-restoration fixture with an explicit seed. Verify listing and direct launch before and after restoration, seed delivery to the real registration, both wrong story answers, the same-round retry, `NEW`, malformed input, save round-trip, reward idempotency and the receipt when another door has already awarded the shared fact. Test that a failed save does not commit the story award or its checkpoint. Retain the unrelated slot and profile data across the round-trip.
- Extend `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` with one `Signal Hunter` case using `seedSaveOnce` and the local keyboard helpers. Seed a v2 save with a fixed profile seed, Episode 000 designation and the approved restoration fact. Leave the Hunter slot and manifest fact absent. Drive the BBS connection, designation, `DOORS`, `OPEN signal-hunter`, a practice selection, scans and the correct submission by keyboard. Freeze the expected evidence and candidate for the chosen seed after independently applying the printed rule. Assert the rendered scan values, practice success, `EXIT`, signed-in main menu and `BBS>` focus. Complete the canonical story route and reload, then check the receipt, round progress and single reward in the real save. The existing workflow discovers the test.

## HANDOFF

### Entry points and files

- Modify the registration surface at `CodeDoorRegistration.load` (`src/doors/contract.ts:84`), `createDoorHost.launch` (`src/doors/host.ts:43`), and `CODE_DOORS` (`src/doors/code-doors.ts:4`). Keep `createDoorRegistry` (`src/doors/registry.ts:9`), `createBbsDoorSession.dispatch` (`src/bbs/door-session.ts:47`) and `createBbsScene` (`src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:9`) as existing integration seams.
- Create the three door modules and three content screens in steps 1–2. Create the two door unit suites in steps 1 and 4, and extend `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:20,47` using `tests/e2e/helpers.ts:5` and the existing `/signal-lost/` fixture (`tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:18`). Reuse the save round-trip and host setup pattern in `tests/unit/doors.test.ts:32–75,154–175,289–332`. The new door tests belong under `tests/unit/signal-hunter` so Vitest's existing include discovers them.
- Checked each proposed new path with `test -e` against the supplied approved source snapshot. All eight files were absent, and the snapshot has no Git metadata by design (`.swarm/prompts/developer.md:22–24`). Recheck if the coordinator supplies a different base. There are no planned file removals.

### Focused verification commands

```sh
npx vitest run tests/unit/signal-hunter
npx vitest run tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/signal.test.ts
npm run content:validate
npx prettier --check src/doors/code-doors.ts src/doors/contract.ts src/doors/host.ts src/doors/signal-hunter 'content/screens/signal-hunter-*.json' tests/unit/signal-hunter tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts
npx eslint src/doors/code-doors.ts src/doors/contract.ts src/doors/host.ts src/doors/signal-hunter tests/unit/signal-hunter tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts
npx tsc --noEmit
npx playwright test tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts --list --grep 'Signal Hunter'
```

`TEST_PLAN.md` assigns the developer checks, the tester's independent review, and the runtime browser check. Treat this handoff as source evidence for review. The approved WorkUnit, gates and coordinator validation policy govern execution.

### Checked assumptions and when to reopen

- Verified that the host already has the persisted seed at the lazy call site, existing loaders ignore arguments, and no existing test calls a registration loader directly. Verified missing restoration from the authored grant inventory and empty code catalog. Verified the typed command path, production asset interception and CI discovery from the source files above.
- Reopen if the new base still lacks a reachable restore action, the manifest fact differs between the two routes, or a required change goes beyond registration in shared code. Reopen if a public-evidence solver finds ambiguity or if the browser requires a change to the host keyboard contract. Fix generation or evidence inside the door when that is sufficient.

### What this change breaks

Repository search covered `CODE_DOORS`, `CodeDoorRegistration`, `.load(`, `hasFact`, `relay-trivia`, SPOOL-02, and the door and browser templates.

- `src/doors/host.ts:49` is the sole existing call site of `registration.load()` and must pass the saved seed. `src/doors/registry.ts:13–24`, the Relay Trivia adapter there, and the no-argument loaders in `tests/unit/doors.test.ts:117–122,389–418`, `tests/unit/access.test.ts:85–105` and `tests/unit/content.test.ts:342–372` retain their behavior and declarations.
- `tests/unit/doors.test.ts:178–194` asserts the fact-only callback API. Preserve it. `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:481–489` derives entries from the registry. Preserve it and keep Episode 000-only saves ineligible for Signal Hunter. `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:47–114,281–293` asserts Relay Trivia behavior and its exact flags. Preserve those journeys and append a standalone case with its own storage setup.
- `docs/architecture.md:53–64` describes lazy code registration, fact-only callbacks and terminal exit. Preserve that contract. `docs/game-design.md:157–185` fixes the canon and `content/doors/relay-trivia.json:2–12` fixes existing trivia metadata. Preserve both. `tests/unit/signal.test.ts:22–79` and `tests/e2e/analyzer.spec.ts:3–32` preserve the Episode 000 analyzer behavior.
- `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:1–25`, `playwright.config.ts:3–14`, the content authoring guide and the issue templates have no Signal Hunter-specific assumptions. Preserve their existing discovery, schema and workflow behavior.

# Issue 31 test plan

The supplied base lacks a playable SPOOL-02 restoration fact producer. The door's pure generation, analysis and command behavior can be specified directly. Production registration and its browser journey require the corrected approved base described in `PLAN.md`. A seeded post-restoration test save verifies the door's behavior after that transition. Separately verify from source that the shipped transition actually grants the fact.

## Acceptance coverage

Numbers follow `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:27–32`. Commands D1–D7 and the CI command are defined below.

| # | Approved criterion | Verification and current coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | At least three difficulties differ in the analysis they require, not only in noise level | **D1** runs `scenarios.test.ts` and `door.test.ts`. The scenario suite proves a louder raw-power decoy for `EASY`, matching pulse totals but different phase behavior for `MEDIUM`, and equal pulse totals and valid pairs with differing decoded signatures for `HARD`. The door suite selects all three difficulties and checks keyboard command descriptors, named measurements, the full numbered trace and the printed rule required for each. The local logic is plan-ready. |
| 2 | A generator test proves the same seed gives the same scenario, and a solver test proves at least 200 seeds per difficulty each have exactly one valid solution, reachable with the door's tools | **D1** runs named determinism and uniqueness cases in `scenarios.test.ts`. For each of seeds `0..199` and `0xffffffff` at each difficulty, generate twice from the same seed, difficulty and ordinal and deep-compare all readings. Enumerate every accepted candidate ID with a test-side solver using the same readings and rules the screen presents. Apply the production adjudicator to all candidates and assert the same singleton. Cover ordinals `0` and `1` in the sweep and add the uint32 rollover case. The door suite independently reads and solves at least one rendered trace per difficulty through `SCAN` and `SUBMIT`. The local logic is plan-ready. |
| 3 | Wrong answers get informative feedback, and a player can retry or request a new seeded scenario | **D1** runs the real door command sequences in `door.test.ts`. For each practice mode, submit a known decoy, check the failed pulse, phase or signature rule, `RETRY`, compare all trace readings before and after, and solve the same round. In a separate wrong-answer path use `NEW`, compare the changed readings and solve the new round. Check wrong-node H1 and damaged-signature H2 keep all story cards visible and award no fact. Practice command behavior is plan-ready. The registered story path needs the corrected gate. |
| 4 | Repeat play yields new scenarios while story rewards are granted only once, with progress restored after a reload | **D1** runs the real registry, host and serialized store cases, **D3** validates the registered gate, and **Browser tests** adds real localStorage evidence. Verify the door is unavailable before the restoration fact, and available with it in either FORGE state. Win practice before acquiring the manifest, verify zero story rewards, submit H3 and count one shared reward, then advance and solve another seeded round. Reload via a fresh save session and host. Verify the current mode, per-mode progress, regenerated readings and receipt. Reopen a separate save with the shared reward already present and no door slot, and check it displays the same receipt and leaves the saved fact count at one. Include a refused write and an invalid or mismatched slot without touching unrelated saved data. Production availability and integration remain blocked on the approved prerequisite. |
| 5 | A browser test in the `Browser tests` workflow solves one fixed-seed scenario by keyboard and returns to the BBS | **D7** checks discovery of the new `Signal Hunter` test. **Browser tests** runs it on Ubuntu/Chromium against the production build and existing Pages fixture. Load an eligible v2 save with a fixed profile seed. Use only keyboard actions to connect, sign in, open the door, select practice, scan visible data, submit the fixed answer, and exit. Assert focus and the signed-in menu. Complete the separate canonical route, reload using the same saved bytes and verify practice and manifest state. Runtime verification is external to the agent sandbox, and the production build requires the corrected gate. |
| 6 | `npx vitest run` with the door's test path validates the door alone | **D1** runs `npx vitest run tests/unit/signal-hunter` using the Node include in `vite.config.ts:5–10`. Confirm only `scenarios.test.ts` and `door.test.ts` are selected, and the latter tests the real shipped catalog and door independently of other suites. Its pure half is plan-ready and registered coverage needs the corrected base. |

### Required evidence within the focused tests

- A uniqueness assertion must compare two independently computed sets of candidates. The test-side solver reads reference and measured values, the documented cutoff and goal, and the printed signature for `HARD`. It never reads a planted candidate, an internal pulse mask or the production diagnostic result while computing its candidates. Verify the `SCAN` renderer exposes every solver input. The candidate command domain is exactly one of `A`, `B`, `C` in practice or `H1`, `H2`, `H3` in the story view. Reject incomplete, unknown and mixed-view commands without awarding progress.
- Assert that `NEW` preserves progress in the other modes, changes data beyond the displayed round number, and produces identical next readings when driven from identical saved seed, difficulty and ordinal. Compare different seeded saves through the actual registration to catch a constant seed passed at launch. Check `RETRY` after a wrong answer leaves the ordinal and readings intact. Validate retention of an in-progress round and a solved round across new save sessions, including `EXIT` followed by a fresh launch.
- For story payout, assert no fact change on scans, `NEW`, a practice solve, H1, H2 or unknown input. The H3 write contains both the validated door slot and the one shared fact. Repeated H3, later practice wins and reload leave one fact and preserve unrelated bytes and progress. A refused write leaves the prior fact set and slot intact and returns through the existing BBS error behavior. Check the `DOORS` listing and direct `OPEN signal-hunter` both before and after restoration.
- In Playwright use the keyboard helpers and the accessible prompt and log. Use a fixed expected trace and answer derived from the printed rule without importing Hunter generation, grading, or internal state helpers. Wait for the latest door output, use `EXIT`, assert the latest system block and the focused `BBS>` input. Assert the actual post-reload receipt and saved fact without reseeding after reload. Capture evidence from the `Browser tests` workflow on the candidate commit.

## Developer-owned focused checks

Run with the authorized Node 24 dependencies for the corrected candidate. The configured agent path is isolated Linux/Codex on SwarmOS's native backend (`.swarm/config.yaml:16–18,59–67`). Vitest runs in Node and exercises the real host and registration, with an in-memory `SaveStorage` boundary. The coordinator provides prepared dependencies where permitted. Capture subprocess output in the sandbox temporary directory and summarize the results in `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

| ID | Command | Expected evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | `npx vitest run tests/unit/signal-hunter` | Only the door's two files run. Record seed count per level and named results for generator, solver, commands, rewards and persistence. |
| D2 | `npx vitest run tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/signal.test.ts` | Existing fact-only callbacks, host failure and settlement behavior, Relay Trivia, and Episode 000 signal controls pass. |
| D3 | `npm run content:validate` | Content validation recognizes the authored restoration fact and accepts the shared reward metadata. Source review verifies the gameplay path that grants the entry fact. The CLI and production build use the same validation (`scripts/content-plugin.ts:6–17`). |
| D4 | `npx prettier --check src/doors/code-doors.ts src/doors/contract.ts src/doors/host.ts src/doors/signal-hunter 'content/screens/signal-hunter-*.json' tests/unit/signal-hunter tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` | Formatting of changed files. |
| D5 | `npx eslint src/doors/code-doors.ts src/doors/contract.ts src/doors/host.ts src/doors/signal-hunter tests/unit/signal-hunter tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` | Static diagnostics on changed TypeScript. |
| D6 | `npx tsc --noEmit` | Type-check lifecycle registration consumers, JSON imports and tests. |
| D7 | `npx playwright test tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts --list --grep 'Signal Hunter'` | Discovery of the fixed-seed scenario by name in the configured Chromium project. This is discovery evidence. |

Each focused check is expected to take under five minutes. Record the exact commands, results, elapsed times, the source-tree identity and the toolchain used. Repeat only for relevant source changes, an observed failure or an unresolved coverage concern, and record the reason.

## Tester-owned independent review and reuse

1. Check the actual restoration producer in the corrected base and trace its persisted fact through `createDoorRegistry`, registration, the seed supplied by `createDoorHost.launch`, and idempotent reward persistence. Review the diff against the authorized base for door-local changes and the narrow registration contract edit.
2. Independently follow each published analysis rule from the generated evidence through the screen and `SUBMIT`. Check the enumerated answer domain, the seed count and unit test independence. Trace `NEW`, `RETRY`, `EXIT`, a restored session, and both reward routes from the implementation and tests. Review the keyboard spec and the unchanged CI configuration for actual keystrokes, visible output, stable expected answer, save restoration and suite discovery.
3. Reuse applicable passing D1–D7 results from `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Record, by criterion, the evidence reference and reuse decision in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`. Rerun a specific D command only for relevant changes, a failure or a gap the source review cannot resolve. Cite its trigger, output, elapsed time and applicability. Use `external` for criterion 5 when the Chromium runtime is still pending and identify the existing Ubuntu `Browser tests` job. Report missing local evidence as unverified. Use the required acceptance-evidence block from `.swarm/prompts/tester.md:10–20`.

For agent evidence, match the approved base and candidate commit when available, plus Node version and dependency lock identity. In snapshots without Git metadata, record a reproducible sorted path and SHA-256 listing of applicable source, tests, content and configuration inputs, including the lockfile and browser config for the relevant checks. The tester compares the inputs relevant to each result before reusing it. For CI and coordinator evidence, record the checked-out candidate SHA and workflow or trusted policy identity.

## Coordinator policy and browser CI

After the roles finish, the coordinator runs the complete trusted-base policy in `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1–13` once on the final candidate. Record the coordinator result in the authoritative validation artifact. Developer and tester evidence is advisory. Claim-bound validation and publication remain coordinator-owned.

| Check that may exceed five minutes | Owner | Planning estimate | Evidence, identity and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete trusted-base required policy, including `npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund && npm test` (15 min timeout). The same policy includes format, lint and build, each with a 5 min timeout. | coordinator | 10–30 min combined allowance | Authoritative `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md` and coordinator result for the final candidate SHA and trusted-base policy revision. Publication and maintainer review use this record for that candidate. |
| `npm run test:e2e` in `Browser tests`, including the new keyboard case. The workflow installs dependencies and Chromium, and Playwright global setup builds the production site. | CI | 5–15 min estimated, 30 min job timeout | PR check `Browser tests / e2e`, step logs for the candidate SHA, and the checked-in workflow revision. Tester and maintainer reference that result when available. Agents leave Chromium execution to this job. |

The browser test uses the existing bundle at `/signal-lost/` by request interception. The sandbox's native shell can inspect the browser source and discover the spec through D7. Chromium execution is assigned to CI by `.swarm/rules/lessons.md:10–12` and `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11–25`.
